OCTOBER FIELD LOG — CAT HEAD AREA, LAKE MARION

This is a retrospective of our firsthand October fishing trips, not a claim that the same fish are holding there today. October's fishing gave us a documented starting point for evaluating the seasonal move into November.

OCTOBER 5 — Our trip produced approximately 240 pounds of catfish, including four fish over 50 pounds. Wind was reported around 7 mph from the north-northeast to north-northwest. These are trip totals, not a lakewide catch forecast.

OCTOBER 13 — Fishing near Cat Head, morning surface water temperature was about 75.7°F. Bait was observed in approximately 10–18 feet of water. The recorded catch included a 6-pound channel catfish and an 8-pound blue catfish, followed by a blue reported around 40 pounds later in the trip.

OCTOBER 21 — Near Cat Head, water temperature ranged from approximately 70.3°F to 72.8°F during the trip. We caught blue catfish weighing approximately 30 and 25 pounds in about 18 feet of water, and later a blue around 40 pounds in approximately 22 feet on an upslope.

WHAT THE LOG TELLS US — During the documented October outings, productive water included bait-related structure and depth changes in the upper-teen to low-20-foot range. The October 21 upslope catch shows why the relationship between contours can matter as much as any single depth. These results document where and how we fished on those dates; they do not establish a current bite at Cat Head or across Lake Marion.

NEXT STEP — November coverage will investigate a new location and compare its contours, bait, water conditions, sonar observations and actual fishing results against this October baseline. Public reports explain the general-area structure and reasoning; exact GPS positions and advanced tactics are available to Master Fisherman Patreon supporters.

DIVERSION CANAL FLOW ASSESSMENT — November 16, 2026 (11:55 a.m. EST)

STATUS: ACTUAL CANAL FLOW NOT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED. Santee Cooper's operational page reports data last updated November 16, 2026, with latest DAILY elevations for November 15 (one-day reporting lag, not instantaneous November 16 measurements). Individual lake gauge observation times and common vertical datum were not independently reconciled. No direct Diversion Canal current, velocity or discharge measurement was verified.

OPERATOR-REPORTED DAILY ELEVATIONS (feet; not independently established as simultaneous, same-datum readings): November 15 Lake Marion 74.19 and Lake Moultrie 74.14, nominal difference Marion minus Moultrie +0.05 ft. November 14 Marion 74.22 and Moultrie 74.21, nominal difference +0.01 ft. Marion declined 0.03 ft and Moultrie declined 0.07 ft; the nominal difference widened 0.04 ft. These are arithmetic comparisons of daily operator figures, NOT a verified instantaneous hydraulic head. November 16 simultaneous lake elevations and actual canal flow remain unknown.

OPERATIONS (operator page updated November 16; TENTATIVE, not verified actual generation): Jefferies Hydro November 16 2 a.m.–10 a.m.; November 17 6 a.m.–midnight. St. Stephen not scheduled November 16 or 17. November 15 daily facility discharge table reports Jefferies 4,964 and St. Stephen 0 (units not independently reconciled here); these are facility entries, NOT Diversion Canal flow observations. Do not assume Jefferies or St. Stephen generation proves canal discharge.

INTERPRETATION — CONDITIONAL INFERENCE ONLY: If Marion and Moultrie elevations share a comparable datum and represent equivalent times, the nominal higher Marion level would be consistent with a potential Marion-to-Moultrie hydraulic gradient. A small +0.05 ft nominal difference, despite widening since November 14, cannot reliably establish current direction or plausible current strength without matched gauge readings and canal observations. Wind setup and operations may change conditions. Direction and strength of canal current are NOT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED; no qualitative strength claim is supported.

Independent timestamp/datum reconciliation and direct canal flow not obtained. Replaces November 15 commentary.
level_analysis: Daily lake-level readings above are published with USGS station timestamps. Review each gauge's vertical datum before comparing Lake Marion and Lake Moultrie. Water movement and reservoir operations require separate verification; elevation alone cannot establish canal discharge.
wind_analysis: The hourly wind forecast above provides broad guidance, but wind exposure varies by fetch, shoreline orientation, gusts and travel route. Check the selected forecast area, recheck conditions before launching, and do not treat a forecast as a measured on-water reading.
temperature_analysis: WATER TEMPERATURE REPORT — November 16, 2026 (8:54 a.m. EST). The ATSC conditions dashboard screenshot supplied this morning displays Lake Marion Pineville USGS 02171000 bottom-water temperature 61.3°F, observed November 16 at 7:45 a.m. EST, and Lake Moultrie Moncks Corner USGS 02172002 downstream tailrace temperature 62.8°F, observed November 16 at 7:45 a.m. EST. Both displayed observations were approximately 69 minutes old at preparation time. These readings are transcribed from the site screenshot, NOT independently confirmed against the primary USGS API during this run because the primary feed could not be retrieved. No verified 24-hour historical pair was obtained, so no 24-hour change is asserted. The two measurements represent different environments: a bottom-water station at Pineville and downstream tailrace water at Moncks Corner, NOT lake-wide surface temperatures. Cooler-season changes can influence bait distribution and blue catfish activity, but neither these two readings nor their difference proves where fish are holding or feeding. Check current timestamps and readings on the live dashboard before use: https://atsclakes.com/#conditions .
